sections.subtopic: Systems of Units and SI Units
sections.title: A measurement is a number and a unit

board_events.text: A measurement = a number + a unit
"I bought a table that's five long."  Five WHAT?
To measure = to ask: how many times does my standard fit into this thing?

board_events.caption: The same table, two rulers: 3.5 m or 350 cm

board_events.text: Switch to a SMALLER unit and the number gets BIGGER.
3 m and 300 cm are the same wall. Only the ruler changed.
A measurement is a RATIO: size of the thing / size of your reference.
Drop either word and the sentence becomes nonsense.

segments.text: <curious> Let me start with something that sounds far too obvious to be physics. Every measurement you will ever make is a sentence with exactly two words in it: a number, and a unit.

Imagine you call up a friend in another city and say, I just bought a table that is five long. Five what? Five feet, five metres, five hand-spans? The number five, sitting there alone, tells him absolutely nothing.

Now here is the deeper idea sitting underneath. When you measure something, you are secretly asking one single question: how many times does my chosen standard fit into this thing? That is all a measurement ever is.

Look at the board. The table swallows the metre stick three and a half times, so we say the table is three point five metres. Measure that same table with ten centimetre steps instead, and you count three hundred and fifty of them.
Nothing about the table changed. Only the ruler changed. And notice which way it moved: you switched to a smaller unit, and the number got bigger, because more of the small unit fits inside.
Three metres and three hundred centimetres are the same wall. The physical size is fixed by nature. The number is only your report of how many times your unit fitted in.
So a measurement is really a ratio, the size of the thing divided by the size of your reference. Hold on to that word, ratio. It is the seed of every unit conversion you will ever do.
And the practical lesson is sharp. Drop either word, the number or the unit, and the whole sentence collapses. In physics, a naked number is never an answer.
<curious> चलो एक ऐसी बात से शुरू करते हैं जो physics कहलाने के लिए ज़्यादा ही obvious लगती है। कोई भी measurement असल में सिर्फ़ दो शब्दों का sentence है — एक number, और एक unit।
सोचो तुमने दूसरे शहर में दोस्त को call किया और कहा, यार मैंने एक table खरीदा है जो five लंबा है। Five what? Five feet, five metre, या five hand-span? अकेला पड़ा हुआ number कुछ भी नहीं बताता।
अब इसके नीचे की असली idea समझो। जब तुम कुछ measure करते हो, तो चुपचाप एक ही सवाल पूछ रहे होते हो — मेरा chosen standard इस चीज़ में कितनी बार fit होता है? बस, measurement इतना ही है।
Board देखो। Table, metre stick को साढ़े तीन बार निगल जाता है, तो हम कहते हैं table साढ़े तीन metre का है। वही table दस centimetre के steps से नापो, तो तीन सौ पचास steps निकलेंगे।
Table में कुछ नहीं बदला। सिर्फ़ ruler बदला। और direction ध्यान से देखो — unit छोटी की, तो number बड़ा हो गया, क्योंकि छोटी unit ज़्यादा बार अंदर fit होती है।
तीन metre और तीन सौ centimetre — बिल्कुल same wall है। Physical size nature ने fix कर रखा है। Number तो बस तुम्हारी report है कि unit कितनी बार fit हुई।
तो measurement असल में एक ratio है — चीज़ का size, divided by तुम्हारे reference का size। इस शब्द ratio को पकड़ कर रखो। यही हर unit conversion का बीज है।
और practical lesson बहुत तीखा है। Number या unit, कोई भी एक हटा दो, पूरा sentence बेकार हो जाता है। Physics में नंगा number कभी answer नहीं होता।

sections.title: Base and derived quantities: seven notes, endless songs

board_events.text: Base quantities vs derived quantities
We do NOT need a separate fundamental standard for everything. That would be chaos.
Pick a few founding members = BASE (fundamental) quantities. Build the rest from them.

board_events.caption: Seven base units fan out into every derived unit

board_events.text: speed = length / time.   force = mass x length / time squared.   These are DERIVED.
Like a language: a few root words (base) make an entire dictionary (derived).
Seven base + two supplementary. The supplementary pair are NOT base units.
The choice of base quantities is CONVENTION, not nature.

segments.text: Now, we could have picked a separate fundamental standard for every single quantity in physics. A standard for speed, another for force, another for pressure. Think about how insane that would be. Total chaos.

So scientists did something much smarter. They picked a small handful of quantities to act as the founding members, and agreed to build absolutely everything else out of those. Those founding members are the base, or fundamental, quantities.

Length, mass and time are the obvious three. Speed? That is just length per time. Force? That is mass times length per time squared. Anything built out of the base ones is called a derived quantity, and its unit is a derived unit.

Look at the board. In the middle sit the seven S I base units — metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, candela — and every arrow fanning out is a derived unit assembled from them. Speed, force, energy, power, pressure, charge, density. All of them, children of those seven.
It works exactly like a language. A few root words, and out of them you construct an entire dictionary. You never need a brand new alphabet for every new word.

<excited> Picture the seven base units as the seven notes of Indian classical music — sa, re, ga, ma, pa, dha, ni. Just seven notes, and yet every raga, every Bollywood song, every symphony is built by combining them. That is exactly what these seven do for physics.

Notice the box sitting off to one side, deliberately not connected: the supplementary units, radian and steradian. They come along with the S I, but they are not base units, and treating them as if they were will corrupt your work later.

And one honest confession before we move on. The choice of these seven is a matter of convention, not of nature. There is nothing sacred about length and time. You could build a perfectly good system where speed and time are fundamental and length becomes derived. The seven are simply what the world agreed on.
अब हम चाहते तो physics की हर एक quantity के लिए अलग fundamental standard रख सकते थे। Speed का अलग, force का अलग, pressure का अलग। ज़रा सोचो कितना पागलपन होता। पूरा chaos।

तो scientists ने कहीं ज़्यादा समझदारी वाला काम किया। उन्होंने मुट्ठी भर quantities चुनीं, जो founding members बनेंगी, और तय किया कि बाकी सब कुछ इन्हीं से बनाया जाएगा। यही base, यानी fundamental, quantities हैं।
Length, mass और time तो obvious तीन हैं। Speed? वो तो बस length per time है। Force? Mass into length per time squared। जो भी base से बनता है उसे derived quantity कहते हैं, और उसकी unit derived unit।

Board देखो। बीच में बैठी हैं सात S I base units — metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, candela — और बाहर निकलता हर arrow एक derived unit है, इन्हीं से जोड़कर बनी हुई। Speed, force, energy, power, pressure, charge, density। सब इन सात की संतान।
यह बिल्कुल किसी language की तरह काम करता है। कुछ root words, और उन्हीं से पूरी dictionary खड़ी हो जाती है। हर नए शब्द के लिए नई alphabet की ज़रूरत नहीं पड़ती।

<excited> इन सात base units को Indian classical music के सात सुरों की तरह देखो — सा, रे, ग, म, प, ध, नि। सिर्फ़ सात सुर, और फिर भी हर राग, हर Bollywood song, हर symphony इन्हीं को मिलाकर बनती है। Physics के लिए ये सात बिल्कुल यही करते हैं।

एक box किनारे पर अलग रखा है, जानबूझकर connect नहीं किया गया — supplementary units, radian और steradian। ये S I के साथ आती हैं, लेकिन base units नहीं हैं, और इन्हें base मान लेना आगे तुम्हारा काम ख़राब कर देगा।

और आगे बढ़ने से पहले एक ईमानदार बात। इन सातों का चुनाव convention है, nature नहीं। Length और time में कुछ पवित्र नहीं है। तुम चाहो तो ऐसा system बना सकते हो जिसमें speed और time fundamental हों और length derived बन जाए। ये सात बस वो हैं जिन पर दुनिया राज़ी हुई।

sections.title: From FPS to SI: why the world had to standardise

board_events.text: Different people, different founding members
British: FPS (foot, pound, second).  Scientists: CGS (cm, gram, second).  Engineers: MKS.
Same quantity, three different numbers. A pharma lab in Pune, a NASA engineer, a French physicist.

board_events.caption: Local systems converge on SI in 1971; constants take over in 2019

board_events.text: 1971: the world agrees on the Systeme International d'Unites - a rationalised MKS.
A good unit is: well-defined, invariant, reproducible anywhere, imperishable.
2019: the platinum kilogram cylinder was retired. Metal scratches and gathers dust.
Units are now anchored to constants of nature, which never change.

segments.text: Over history, different groups of people picked different founding members, and different sizes for them. The British built the F P S system on the foot, the pound and the second. Scientists liked the C G S system — centimetre, gram, second. Engineers leaned on M K S — metre, kilogram, second.
Each system worked fine inside its own room. The trouble started the moment the rooms had to talk to each other.

A pharma company in Pune, an engineer at N A S A, and a physicist in France would all measure the very same thing and write down three completely different numbers. Not because the physics disagreed, but because their rulers did.

Follow the board from left to right. F P S, C G S, M K S — three parallel worlds. And then, in nineteen seventy one, the world finally agreed on one universal standard: the Systeme International d'Unites, which everyone just calls S I. Seven base units, two supplementary units, and it is essentially an upgraded, rationalised M K S.

Now, what actually makes a unit good enough to be a world standard? Four things. It must be well-defined, so nobody argues about what it means. It must be invariant, so it does not drift with time or place or temperature. It must be reproducible anywhere. And it must be imperishable.

Hold that fourth word, imperishable, against how the kilogram used to be defined: by an actual lump of platinum sitting in a vault in France. A lump of metal can get scratched. It can gain a film of dust. It can very slowly stop being exactly one kilogram.
<whisper> So in two thousand nineteen, the world quietly did something rather beautiful. It threw the cylinder away.

Every base unit is now fixed by assigning an exact numerical value to a constant of nature. Constants do not scratch, do not gather dust, and do not need a vault. Anchor the constants, and any lab anywhere in the cosmos can rebuild the units from scratch.

इतिहास में अलग-अलग लोगों ने अलग founding members चुने, और उनके अलग sizes भी। British ने F P S system बनाया — foot, pound, second पर। Scientists को C G S पसंद था — centimetre, gram, second। Engineers M K S पर टिके — metre, kilogram, second।
हर system अपने कमरे के अंदर ठीक चलता था। दिक्कत उस पल शुरू हुई जब कमरों को आपस में बात करनी पड़ी।

Pune की pharma company, N A S A का engineer, और France का physicist — तीनों बिल्कुल same चीज़ measure करते और तीन एकदम अलग numbers लिखते। इसलिए नहीं कि physics अलग थी, बल्कि इसलिए कि उनके rulers अलग थे।

Board पर बाएँ से दाएँ चलो। F P S, C G S, M K S — तीन parallel दुनिया। और फिर उन्नीस सौ इकहत्तर में दुनिया आख़िरकार एक universal standard पर राज़ी हुई: Systeme International d'Unites, जिसे सब बस S I कहते हैं। सात base units, दो supplementary units, और असल में यह upgraded, rationalised M K S ही है।

अब सवाल — कोई unit world standard बनने लायक़ अच्छी कब कहलाती है? चार शर्तें। वो well-defined हो, ताकि उसके मतलब पर झगड़ा न हो। Invariant हो, यानी time, place या temperature के साथ न खिसके। कहीं भी reproducible हो। और imperishable हो।

अब इस चौथे शब्द को पुराने kilogram की definition के सामने रखो: France की एक तिजोरी में रखा platinum का असली टुकड़ा। धातु के टुकड़े पर scratch आ सकता है। उस पर धूल की परत जम सकती है। वो धीरे-धीरे exactly एक kilogram रहना बंद कर सकता है।
<whisper> तो दो हज़ार उन्नीस में दुनिया ने चुपचाप एक बेहद ख़ूबसूरत काम किया। उसने वो cylinder फेंक दिया।

अब हर base unit nature के किसी constant को exact numerical value देकर fix की जाती है। Constants पर scratch नहीं आता, उन पर धूल नहीं जमती, और उन्हें तिजोरी नहीं चाहिए। Constants को anchor कर दो, और cosmos की कोई भी lab units को शुरू से दोबारा खड़ा कर सकती है।

board_events.text: Step 2: write each piece in base units. Force from F = ma is kg x m s^{-2}. Area is m^2.
The REASONING protects you, not the memorised result.
In an exam you WILL meet a quantity you have never seen. This chain is the only safe route.

segments.text: Since this subtopic has no formal derivation, what you must own instead are three logical procedures. Here is the first, and it is the one that saves you when a question throws an unfamiliar quantity at you.
Step one: always start from the defining relation of the quantity. Not from a memorised unit — from the definition. Take pressure. Pressure is defined as force per unit area.
There it is on the board: P equals F over A. That single line is the whole starting point, and everything else is just bookkeeping from here.
Now follow the chain in the picture. We take the definition at the top, and we break each piece on the right hand side into base units, one at a time, until nothing unfamiliar is left.

Step two. Force is not a base unit, so we crack it open too: force comes from F equals m a, so it is kilogram times metre per second squared, that is, kilogram metre per second squared. Area is straightforward — metre squared. Why bother? Because every derived unit must ultimately trace back to the seven base units. That is the entire point of a coherent system.

Step three, combine. Kilogram metre per second squared, divided by metre squared, gives kilogram per metre per second squared. And that is the pascal, written purely in base units. Notice the metre: one on top, two below, leaving metre to the power minus one.
Here is the part I really want you to take away. The memorised result is not what protects you. The reasoning is.

Because in an exam you will sometimes meet a quantity you have genuinely never seen before. No memorised list will save you there. This base-unit chain — definition, break each piece, combine — is the only safe way to handle it.
इस subtopic में कोई formal derivation नहीं है, इसलिए तुम्हें तीन logical procedures पक्की करनी हैं। यह पहली है, और यही वो है जो exam में अनजान quantity आने पर तुम्हें बचाती है।
Step one: हमेशा quantity के defining relation से शुरू करो। रटी हुई unit से नहीं — definition से। Pressure लो। Pressure की definition है force per unit area।
Board पर वही है: P equals F over A। बस यही एक line पूरा starting point है, और उसके बाद सब कुछ सिर्फ़ bookkeeping है।
अब picture में chain को follow करो। ऊपर definition लेते हैं, और right hand side के हर टुकड़े को एक-एक करके base units में तोड़ते हैं, जब तक कुछ भी अनजाना न बचे।

Step two। Force base unit नहीं है, तो उसे भी खोलते हैं: force आता है F equals m a से, यानी kilogram into metre per second squared, यानी kilogram metre per second squared। Area सीधा है — metre squared। यह मेहनत क्यों? क्योंकि हर derived unit को आख़िर में उन सात base units तक पहुँचना ही होगा। Coherent system का पूरा मतलब यही है।

Step three, combine करो। Kilogram metre per second squared, divided by metre squared, बनता है kilogram per metre per second squared। और यही pascal है, पूरी तरह base units में लिखा हुआ। Metre को ध्यान से देखो: एक ऊपर, दो नीचे, बचा metre to the power minus one।
अब वो हिस्सा जो मैं सच में चाहता हूँ तुम ले जाओ। रटा हुआ result तुम्हें नहीं बचाता। Reasoning बचाती है।

क्योंकि exam में कभी-कभी ऐसी quantity आ जाएगी जो तुमने सचमुच कभी देखी ही नहीं। वहाँ कोई रटी हुई list काम नहीं आएगी। यह base-unit chain — definition लो, हर टुकड़ा तोड़ो, combine करो — वहाँ इकलौता सुरक्षित रास्ता है।

sections.subtopic: Systems of Units and SI Units
sections.title: Procedures B and C: converting, and building a system from scratch

board_events.text: PROCEDURE B - convert a value between two systems
Step 1: find the dimensional formula. Students SKIP this - and then get conversions wrong.
Why the powers? The dimension counts how many times that unit PARTICIPATES.
Sanity check: converting to a SMALLER unit must give a LARGER number.
PROCEDURE C - build a new system of units
Declare some quantities fundamental. Write the target as a product of their powers.
Equate dimensions on both sides and solve for the exponents. This is the 2019 trick.

segments.text: Procedure B is how you carry a value across from one system of units into another, and it has exactly three steps.

Step one: find the dimensional formula of the quantity. It looks like M to the a, L to the b, T to the c. This is the step students skip because it feels like a detour — and skipping it is precisely why their conversions come out wrong.

Step two: apply the master relation on the board. The new number equals the old number, times the mass ratio raised to a, times the length ratio raised to b, times the time ratio raised to c. Notice: old over new inside every bracket.

Now, why on earth are those ratios raised to powers? Because the dimension counts how many times that unit participates in the quantity. If length appears cubed — as it does in a volume, or in a density — then the length ratio must be cubed too. The exponent is not decoration; it is a headcount.

Step three, and please do not skip this one either: sanity check the direction. Converting into a smaller unit must give you a larger number. If your answer breaks that rule, you have inverted a ratio somewhere. Go back and flip it.
Procedure C is the most beautiful of the three, because it is the actual trick behind the two thousand nineteen redefinition.

Step one: identify which quantities you are declaring fundamental. In the real S I, it is fundamental constants — the speed of light, the Planck constant — that get declared fixed. Step two: express the unit you want as a product of powers of those fundamentals, with unknown exponents sitting on top.

Step three: equate dimensions on both sides and solve for the exponents. Each of M, L and T hands you one equation, so three unknowns is exactly solvable. This is pure dimensional bookkeeping, and the philosophy behind it is glorious: anchor a few unchanging constants, and every unit follows automatically, reproducible in any lab in the cosmos.
Procedure B वो तरीक़ा है जिससे तुम किसी value को एक system of units से दूसरे में ले जाते हो, और इसमें ठीक तीन steps हैं।

Step one: quantity का dimensional formula निकालो। वो दिखता है M to the a, L to the b, T to the c। यही वो step है जिसे students छोड़ देते हैं क्योंकि लगता है फ़ालतू का चक्कर है — और इसी को छोड़ने की वजह से उनके conversions ग़लत निकलते हैं।

Step two: board पर लिखा master relation लगाओ। नया number बराबर पुराना number, into mass ratio raised to a, into length ratio raised to b, into time ratio raised to c। ध्यान दो: हर bracket के अंदर पुराना ऊपर, नया नीचे।

अब सवाल — इन ratios पर powers आख़िर क्यों? क्योंकि dimension गिनती है कि वो unit quantity में कितनी बार participate करती है। अगर length cube होकर आती है — जैसे volume में, या density में — तो length ratio भी cube होना ही चाहिए। Exponent सजावट नहीं है; वो एक headcount है।

Step three, और इसे भी मत छोड़ना: direction का sanity check। छोटी unit में convert कर रहे हो तो number बड़ा आना ही चाहिए। अगर तुम्हारा answer यह नियम तोड़ रहा है, तो कहीं ratio उलटा हो गया है। वापस जाओ और पलटो।
Procedure C तीनों में सबसे ख़ूबसूरत है, क्योंकि यही दो हज़ार उन्नीस की redefinition के पीछे का असली trick है।

Step one: तय करो कौन सी quantities को fundamental declare कर रहे हो। असली S I में fundamental constants declare होते हैं — speed of light, Planck constant — उन्हें fixed मान लिया जाता है। Step two: जो unit चाहिए उसे उन fundamentals की powers के product की तरह लिखो, ऊपर unknown exponents बैठाकर।

Step three: दोनों तरफ़ dimensions बराबर करो और exponents solve करो। M, L और T — हर एक तुम्हें एक equation देता है, तो तीन unknowns बिल्कुल solvable हैं। यह शुद्ध dimensional bookkeeping है, और इसके पीछे की philosophy शानदार है: कुछ अटल constants anchor कर दो, और हर unit अपने आप निकल आती है, cosmos की किसी भी lab में दोबारा बनाई जा सकती है।

sections.subtopic: Systems of Units and SI Units
sections.title: The seven SI base quantities and their dimensional formulae

board_events.text: The seven SI base quantities
Length = metre (m) = [L].     Mass = kilogram (kg) = [M].     Time = second (s) = [T].
Electric current = ampere (A) = [A].
Thermodynamic temperature = kelvin (K) = [K].
Amount of substance = mole (mol) = [mol].     Luminous intensity = candela (cd) = [cd].
This is a FIXED, MEMORISED list. Never reason it out from intuition.
Charge, force and energy are NOT here. Current is the electrical base quantity.
Every other unit in physics is assembled from these seven.

segments.text: Here is the list itself, and I want you to treat this section as a thing you memorise rather than a thing you understand. Seven base quantities, seven units, seven symbols, seven dimensional formulae.

The first three you already feel in your bones. Length: unit metre, symbol m, dimensional formula capital L in square brackets. Mass: unit kilogram, symbol k g, dimensional formula capital M. Time: unit second, symbol s, dimensional formula capital T.
Fourth, and this is the one students get wrong: electric current. Unit ampere, symbol capital A, dimensional formula capital A in brackets. Current — not charge, not voltage, not resistance. Current.
Fifth, thermodynamic temperature. Unit kelvin, symbol capital K, dimensional formula capital K. And note the word thermodynamic — it is kelvin that is base, not celsius.

Sixth, amount of substance. Unit mole, symbol m o l, dimensional formula mole in brackets. Seventh, luminous intensity. Unit candela, symbol c d, dimensional formula candela in brackets. These last two are the ones people forget even exist.
<whisper> And here is the exam secret. This list is fixed and memorised. It is not something you derive, and it is not something you feel your way to.

Look at what is missing. Charge is not here. Force is not here. Energy is not here. Every single one of them feels fundamental, and every single one of them is derived. For anything electrical, the ampere is the root and everything else grows out of it.
Learn these seven cold, because every other unit in the whole of physics — every newton, every joule, every pascal, every volt — is assembled out of exactly these.
अब list ख़ुद देखते हैं, और मैं चाहता हूँ इस section को समझने की चीज़ नहीं, याद करने की चीज़ मानो। सात base quantities, सात units, सात symbols, सात dimensional formulae।

पहली तीन तो तुम्हें हड्डियों में महसूस होती हैं। Length: unit metre, symbol m, dimensional formula square bracket में capital L। Mass: unit kilogram, symbol k g, dimensional formula capital M। Time: unit second, symbol s, dimensional formula capital T।

चौथी, और यही वो है जिसमें students मार खाते हैं: electric current। Unit ampere, symbol capital A, dimensional formula bracket में capital A। Current — charge नहीं, voltage नहीं, resistance नहीं। Current।
पाँचवीं, thermodynamic temperature। Unit kelvin, symbol capital K, dimensional formula capital K। और यह शब्द thermodynamic ध्यान से देखो — base kelvin है, celsius नहीं।

छठी, amount of substance। Unit mole, symbol m o l, dimensional formula bracket में mole। सातवीं, luminous intensity। Unit candela, symbol c d, dimensional formula bracket में candela। यही आख़िरी दो हैं जिनका होना ही लोग भूल जाते हैं।
<whisper> और यह रहा exam secret। यह list fixed है और रटी जाती है। यह derive करने की चीज़ नहीं है, और अंदाज़े से पहुँचने की तो बिल्कुल नहीं।

अब देखो क्या ग़ायब है। Charge यहाँ नहीं है। Force यहाँ नहीं है। Energy यहाँ नहीं है। इनमें से हर एक fundamental महसूस होती है, और हर एक derived है। Electrical कुछ भी हो, जड़ ampere है और बाकी सब उसी से निकलता है।
इन सातों को पक्का याद करो, क्योंकि पूरी physics की हर दूसरी unit — हर newton, हर joule, हर pascal, हर volt — इन्हीं से जोड़कर बनी है।

sections.title: The two supplementary units: radian and steradian

board_events.text: The two SI supplementary units
ds is the arc length, r is the radius. Length divided by length.

board_events.caption: Plane angle is arc/radius; solid angle is area/radius squared

board_events.text: dA is the area of the patch on a sphere, r is the radius. Area divided by area.
Genuinely DIMENSIONLESS. Never treat them like ordinary base units.

segments.text: Alongside the seven base units, the S I carries two special citizens called the supplementary units. There are only two of them, and they both measure angles.
The first is the plane angle. On the board: d theta equals d s over r. That is the definition of the radian.
In words: take the arc your angle cuts out, and divide it by the radius of the circle. That is it. Arc length divided by radius — a length, divided by a length.

Look at the left half of the picture. There is the radius r running out to the circle, there is the little arc d s riding along the rim, and the angle between them is d theta. On the right half is the same idea one dimension up: a patch of area d A sitting on the surface of a sphere of radius r.
That patch defines the second supplementary unit, the solid angle. d omega equals d A over r squared. This is the steradian, symbol s r.
Again read it as a ratio: the area of the patch on the sphere, divided by the radius squared — which is itself an area. So it is an area, divided by an area.

And now watch what that does to the dimensions. Length over length cancels perfectly. Area over area cancels perfectly. Both come out as M to the zero, L to the zero, T to the zero. Every single dimension is gone.

So here is the point you must not lose. Radian and steradian are genuinely dimensionless, even though they clearly describe something physical. Never treat them as if they were ordinary base units carrying length or area with them. Do that, and every dimensional analysis you attempt afterwards is quietly poisoned.
सात base units के साथ-साथ S I में दो ख़ास नागरिक और चलते हैं, जिन्हें supplementary units कहते हैं। ये सिर्फ़ दो हैं, और दोनों angles नापती हैं।
पहली है plane angle। Board पर: d theta equals d s over r। यही radian की definition है।
शब्दों में: तुम्हारा angle जो arc काटता है उसे लो, और circle की radius से divide कर दो। बस इतना ही। Arc length divided by radius — एक length, divided by एक length।

Picture का बायाँ आधा हिस्सा देखो। वहाँ radius r circle तक जा रही है, किनारे पर छोटा सा arc d s चल रहा है, और उन दोनों के बीच का angle है d theta। दायाँ आधा वही idea एक dimension ऊपर है: radius r वाले sphere की सतह पर बैठा area का एक patch, d A।
वही patch दूसरी supplementary unit define करता है, solid angle। d omega equals d A over r squared। यह steradian है, symbol s r।
इसे भी ratio की तरह पढ़ो: sphere पर patch का area, divided by radius squared — और radius squared ख़ुद एक area है। यानी एक area, divided by एक area।
अब देखो इसका dimensions पर क्या असर पड़ता है। Length बटा length पूरी तरह cancel। Area बटा area पूरी तरह cancel। दोनों निकलते हैं M to the zero, L to the zero, T to the zero। हर एक dimension ग़ायब।

तो यह बात मत खोना। Radian और steradian सचमुच dimensionless हैं, भले ही वो साफ़-साफ़ कुछ physical describe करती हों। इन्हें कभी ordinary base units मत मानो जो अपने साथ length या area लेकर चलती हों। ऐसा किया, तो उसके बाद की हर dimensional analysis चुपचाप ज़हरीली हो जाएगी।

sections.subtopic: Systems of Units and SI Units
sections.title: The 2019 SI: seven defining constants

board_events.text: Every base unit is now fixed by a constant of nature
Seven constants, seven base units. No artifacts, no vaults, no drift.

segments.text: This is the modern face of the S I, and it is worth understanding rather than just memorising. Seven constants of nature, each handed an exact numerical value by decree, and from those seven every base unit falls out.

First, the speed of light in vacuum. c is declared to be two nine nine, seven nine two, four five eight metres per second — exactly, with no uncertainty at all. Fix that number, and you have defined the metre. The metre is now whatever distance light covers in the right sliver of a second.

Second, the caesium hyperfine frequency. Delta nu of caesium is declared to be nine one nine two, six three one, seven seven zero hertz. Count that many oscillations of caesium radiation and you have defined the second.

Third, the Planck constant. h is fixed at six point six two six zero seven zero one five, times ten to the power minus thirty four, joule seconds. That one number is what defines the kilogram now. This is the constant that replaced the platinum cylinder.
Fourth, the elementary charge. e is fixed at one point six zero two one seven six six three four, times ten to the power minus nineteen coulombs, and that defines the ampere.
Fifth, the Boltzmann constant. k B is fixed at one point three eight zero six four nine, times ten to the power minus twenty three, joules per kelvin — and that defines the kelvin.

Sixth and seventh, on the last line. The Avogadro constant, six point zero two two one four zero seven six times ten to the power twenty three per mole, defines the mole. And the luminous efficacy, K c d, fixed at six hundred and eighty three lumens per watt, defines the candela.

Seven constants, seven base units, and a one-to-one match between them. No artifacts. No vaults. No slow drift over decades. This is exactly why the boards and J E E both love asking what the two thousand nineteen redefinition was based on, and the answer is always the same: fixed numerical values of fundamental constants of nature.
यह S I का आधुनिक चेहरा है, और इसे सिर्फ़ रटने से बेहतर है समझना। Nature के सात constants, हर एक को हुक्म से exact numerical value दी गई, और उन्हीं सातों से हर base unit निकल आती है।

पहला, vacuum में speed of light। c को declare किया गया है दो नौ नौ, सात नौ दो, चार पाँच आठ metre per second — exactly, बिना किसी uncertainty के। यह number fix करो, और metre define हो गया। Metre अब वो दूरी है जो light second के एक तयशुदा टुकड़े में तय करती है।
दूसरा, caesium hyperfine frequency। Delta nu caesium declare है नौ एक नौ दो, छह तीन एक, सात सात शून्य hertz। Caesium radiation के इतने oscillations गिनो, second define हो गया।

तीसरा, Planck constant। h fix है छह point छह दो छह शून्य सात शून्य एक पाँच, into ten to the power minus thirty four, joule second। वही एक number अब kilogram define करता है। यही वो constant है जिसने platinum cylinder की जगह ली।
चौथा, elementary charge। e fix है एक point छह शून्य दो एक सात छह छह तीन चार, into ten to the power minus nineteen coulomb, और उससे ampere define होता है।
पाँचवाँ, Boltzmann constant। k B fix है एक point तीन आठ शून्य छह चार नौ, into ten to the power minus twenty three, joule per kelvin — और उससे kelvin define होता है।

छठा और सातवाँ, आख़िरी line पर। Avogadro constant, छह point शून्य दो दो एक चार शून्य सात छह into ten to the power twenty three per mole, mole को define करता है। और luminous efficacy, K c d, छह सौ तिरासी lumen per watt पर fix, candela को define करता है।

सात constants, सात base units, और दोनों के बीच one-to-one match। कोई artifact नहीं। कोई तिजोरी नहीं। दशकों में धीरे-धीरे खिसकना नहीं। इसीलिए boards और J E E दोनों पूछना पसंद करते हैं कि दो हज़ार उन्नीस की redefinition किस पर आधारित थी, और जवाब हमेशा एक ही है: fundamental constants of nature की fixed numerical values।

sections.subtopic: Systems of Units and SI Units
sections.title: Coherent derived units you must know cold

board_events.text: Derived units - built from the base seven
COHERENT: a product/quotient of base units with NO extra numerical factor.
SI is deliberately coherent - which is why conversions inside SI need no awkward constants.

segments.text: Now the derived units — the ones actually built out of the base seven. But before the list, one word you should understand rather than skim past: coherent.

A derived unit is called coherent when it is nothing more than a product or a quotient of base units, with no extra numerical factor bolted on. No stray twos, no conversion constants, nothing. Just base units multiplied and divided.

Force. The unit is the newton, symbol capital N, and it equals kilogram metre per second squared. Dimensional formula: M L T to the minus two. This one comes straight out of F equals m a, exactly as we chased it through in Procedure A.

Energy, and also work, since they share a unit. The joule, symbol capital J, equals kilogram metre squared per second squared. Dimensional formula M L squared T to the minus two. Read it as force times distance and you can see where the extra metre came from.

Power. The watt, symbol capital W, equals kilogram metre squared per second cubed. Dimensional formula M L squared T to the minus three. It is energy per unit time, so the joule simply picks up one more second downstairs.

Pressure. The pascal, symbol P a, equals kilogram per metre per second squared. Dimensional formula M L to the minus one T to the minus two. We derived this one from scratch earlier, and there it is on the board again.

Charge. The coulomb, symbol capital C, equals ampere second. Dimensional formula A T. Notice how short that is — charge is current times time, nothing more. This single line is why charge cannot possibly be a base quantity.

And here is why coherence matters practically. Because the S I is deliberately built to be coherent, conversions inside the S I never need awkward constants. Multiply and divide, and the units simply work. That is a design choice, not an accident.
अब derived units — जो असल में उन सात base से बनी हैं। पर list से पहले एक शब्द जिसे तुम्हें समझना है, ऊपर-ऊपर से पढ़कर छोड़ना नहीं: coherent।

कोई derived unit तब coherent कहलाती है जब वो base units के product या quotient से ज़्यादा कुछ न हो, ऊपर से कोई extra numerical factor न चिपका हो। कोई आवारा two नहीं, कोई conversion constant नहीं, कुछ नहीं। बस base units गुणा और भाग।

Force। Unit है newton, symbol capital N, और यह बराबर है kilogram metre per second squared। Dimensional formula: M L T to the minus two। यह सीधा F equals m a से आता है, ठीक वैसे जैसे हमने Procedure A में पीछा किया था।

Energy, और work भी, क्योंकि दोनों की unit एक है। Joule, symbol capital J, बराबर kilogram metre squared per second squared। Dimensional formula M L squared T to the minus two। इसे force into distance की तरह पढ़ो और extra metre कहाँ से आया, दिख जाएगा।

Power। Watt, symbol capital W, बराबर kilogram metre squared per second cubed। Dimensional formula M L squared T to the minus three। यह energy per unit time है, तो joule बस नीचे एक और second उठा लेता है।
Pressure। Pascal, symbol P a, बराबर kilogram per metre per second squared। Dimensional formula M L to the minus one T to the minus two। इसे हमने पहले शुरू से derive किया था, और वो फिर से board पर है।

Charge। Coulomb, symbol capital C, बराबर ampere second। Dimensional formula A T। देखो कितनी छोटी है — charge है current into time, इससे ज़्यादा कुछ नहीं। यही एक line बताती है कि charge base quantity हो ही नहीं सकती।

और coherence practically क्यों मायने रखता है, यह सुनो। क्योंकि S I को जानबूझकर coherent बनाया गया है, S I के अंदर conversions में कभी अजीब constants नहीं लगते। गुणा-भाग करो, units अपने आप बैठ जाती हैं। यह design का फ़ैसला है, इत्तेफ़ाक़ नहीं।

sections.subtopic: Systems of Units and SI Units
sections.title: Prefixes, practical units, and the master conversion relation

board_events.text: SI prefixes - because physics spans 10^{-15} m to 10^{26} m
Length: 1 angstrom = 10^{-10} m | 1 fermi = 10^{-15} m | 1 AU = 1.496 x 10^{11} m
1 light year = 9.46 x 10^{15} m | 1 parsec = 3.086 x 10^{16} m
Mass: 1 u = 1.66 x 10^{-27} kg | 1 tonne = 10^{3} kg | 1 quintal = 10^{2} kg

segments.text: Physical quantities span an absurd range — from a nucleus at about ten to the minus fifteen metres, out to a far quasar at about ten to the twenty six metres. Rather than drowning in zeros, the S I hands you standard decimal prefixes.

Going up: tera is ten to the twelve, giga is ten to the nine, mega is ten to the six, kilo is ten to the three, hecto is ten squared, deca is ten to the one. These are the ones you already meet in gigabytes and kilometres.

Going down: centi is ten to the minus two, milli is ten to the minus three, micro is ten to the minus six, nano is ten to the minus nine, pico is ten to the minus twelve, femto is ten to the minus fifteen. Notice the base unit never changes — the metre stays the metre. The prefixes are just convenient costumes it wears.

Then there are the practical units — not strictly S I, but accepted, because they are simply handy. For length: one angstrom is ten to the minus ten metres, which is atomic scale. One fermi is ten to the minus fifteen metres, which is nuclear scale. One astronomical unit, written A U, is about one point four nine six times ten to the eleven metres — the Earth to Sun distance.

Bigger still: one light year is about nine point four six times ten to the fifteen metres. One parsec is about three point zero eight six times ten to the sixteen metres. Keep that order in your head — astronomical unit, then light year, then parsec, smallest to largest.

For mass: one atomic mass unit, written u, is about one point six six times ten to the minus twenty seven kilograms. One tonne is ten to the three kilograms. One quintal is ten squared kilograms. And time simply comes off the second — minute, hour, day — but the second remains the base.

Now the single most useful line in this entire subtopic. The physical size of a quantity is fixed by nature, so the product of its numerical value n and its unit size u must be a constant across every system. n one u one equals n two u two.

Unpack that using the dimensional formula M to the a, L to the b, T to the c, and you get the master relation on the last line. The new number equals the old number, times the mass ratio to the power a, the length ratio to the power b, the time ratio to the power c — old over new inside each bracket. Every conversion question you will ever be set is this one line, plus arithmetic.

Physical quantities का range बेतुका बड़ा है — nucleus लगभग ten to the minus fifteen metre पर, और दूर का quasar लगभग ten to the twenty six metre पर। Zeros में डूबने के बजाय S I तुम्हें standard decimal prefixes देता है।

ऊपर की तरफ़: tera है ten to the twelve, giga है ten to the nine, mega है ten to the six, kilo है ten to the three, hecto है ten squared, deca है ten to the one। ये वही हैं जो तुम gigabyte और kilometre में रोज़ मिलते हो।

नीचे की तरफ़: centi है ten to the minus two, milli है ten to the minus three, micro है ten to the minus six, nano है ten to the minus nine, pico है ten to the minus twelve, femto है ten to the minus fifteen। ध्यान दो base unit कभी नहीं बदलती — metre, metre ही रहता है। Prefixes तो बस उसके पहने हुए सुविधाजनक कपड़े हैं।

फिर आती हैं practical units — सख़्ती से S I नहीं, पर accepted, क्योंकि बस काम की हैं। Length के लिए: एक angstrom है ten to the minus ten metre, यानी atomic scale। एक fermi है ten to the minus fifteen metre, यानी nuclear scale। एक astronomical unit, लिखते हैं A U, लगभग एक point चार नौ छह into ten to the eleven metre — Earth से Sun की दूरी।

और बड़ा: एक light year लगभग नौ point चार छह into ten to the fifteen metre। एक parsec लगभग तीन point शून्य आठ छह into ten to the sixteen metre। यह क्रम दिमाग़ में रखो — astronomical unit, फिर light year, फिर parsec, छोटे से बड़े।

Mass के लिए: एक atomic mass unit, लिखते हैं u, लगभग एक point छह छह into ten to the minus twenty seven kilogram। एक tonne है ten to the three kilogram। एक quintal है ten squared kilogram। और time सीधा second से निकलता है — minute, hour, day — पर base second ही रहता है।

अब इस पूरे subtopic की सबसे काम की एक line। किसी quantity का physical size nature ने fix कर रखा है, इसलिए उसकी numerical value n और unit size u का product हर system में constant रहना ही चाहिए। n one u one equals n two u two।

इसे dimensional formula M to the a, L to the b, T to the c के साथ खोलो, और आख़िरी line वाला master relation मिल जाता है। नया number बराबर पुराना number, into mass ratio to the power a, length ratio to the power b, time ratio to the power c — हर bracket में पुराना ऊपर, नया नीचे। तुम्हें जो भी conversion question मिलेगा, वो यही एक line है, प्लस arithmetic।

sections.subtopic: Systems of Units and SI Units
sections.title: Example 1 [CBSE]: the gas constant R in base units

board_events.text: [CBSE Board Level] Express J mol^{-1} K^{-1} in SI base units
Given: the universal gas constant R has SI unit J mol^{-1} K^{-1}.
Step 1 - break down the non-base unit. The joule is NOT a base unit.
Step 2 - substitute back into the unit of R.

board_events.latex: \text{unit of } R = \frac{\mathrm{kg\ m^{2}\ s^{-2}}}{\mathrm{mol}\cdot\mathrm{K}} = \mathrm{kg\ m^{2}\ s^{-2}\ mol^{-1}\ K^{-1}}

board_events.text: mole and kelvin SURVIVE - they are base units and cannot be broken down.
This is Procedure A in action: find the non-base piece, crack it, substitute.

segments.text: First worked example, board level. The universal gas constant R has the S I unit joule per mole per kelvin. Express that unit entirely in terms of the S I base units.
So what are we given? The unit of R is joule per mole per kelvin. That is the whole question. Now scan it against the list of seven and ask which pieces are base and which are impostors.
Mole is base. Kelvin is base. Joule — joule is not on the list. So step one is to break down the non-base unit, and the joule is our only target.

How do we crack the joule? Energy equals work equals force times distance. So a joule is a newton times a metre. And a newton, as we know, is kilogram metre per second squared. Multiply that by one more metre and the joule becomes kilogram metre squared per second squared. There it is on the board.
Step two, substitute back. Wherever the question wrote joule, we now write kilogram metre squared per second squared, and we leave the mole and the kelvin exactly where they sit downstairs.

The unit of R comes out as kilogram metre squared per second squared per mole per kelvin. Written with exponents: kilogram, metre squared, second to the minus two, mole to the minus one, kelvin to the minus one.

Now notice the thing worth noticing. The mole and the kelvin survived untouched. They did not break down into anything, because they are base units — there is nothing underneath them to break into. Only the joule dissolved.

And step back and see what we just did: that was Procedure A, exactly as we set it out. Find the piece that is not base, crack it open using its defining relation, substitute back. No memorisation required — just the chain.
पहला worked example, board level। Universal gas constant R की S I unit है joule per mole per kelvin। इस unit को पूरी तरह S I base units में लिखो।
तो दिया क्या है? R की unit है joule per mole per kelvin। बस यही पूरा सवाल है। अब इसे सात वाली list के सामने रखो और पूछो कौन से टुकड़े base हैं और कौन नक़ली।
Mole base है। Kelvin base है। Joule — joule list में है ही नहीं। तो step one है non-base unit को तोड़ना, और joule ही हमारा इकलौता निशाना है।

Joule को तोड़ें कैसे? Energy equals work equals force into distance। तो एक joule है एक newton into एक metre। और newton, जैसा हमें पता है, kilogram metre per second squared है। उसे एक और metre से गुणा करो और joule बन जाता है kilogram metre squared per second squared। Board पर वही लिखा है।
Step two, वापस substitute करो। जहाँ सवाल में joule लिखा था, अब हम kilogram metre squared per second squared लिखते हैं, और mole तथा kelvin को नीचे बिल्कुल जहाँ थे वहीं छोड़ देते हैं।
R की unit निकलती है kilogram metre squared per second squared per mole per kelvin। Exponents के साथ: kilogram, metre squared, second to the minus two, mole to the minus one, kelvin to the minus one।
अब वो चीज़ देखो जो देखने लायक़ है। Mole और kelvin जस के तस बच गए। वो किसी चीज़ में टूटे ही नहीं, क्योंकि वो base units हैं — उनके नीचे तोड़ने को कुछ है ही नहीं। सिर्फ़ joule घुला।

और पीछे हटकर देखो हमने अभी किया क्या: यह Procedure A था, बिल्कुल वैसा जैसा हमने रखा था। वो टुकड़ा ढूँढो जो base नहीं है, उसे उसके defining relation से खोलो, वापस substitute करो। रटने की ज़रूरत नहीं — बस chain।

sections.title: Example 2 [NEET trap]: which one is a base quantity?

THE TRAP: charge FEELS fundamental. Most students tick (A) on reflex. Wrong.

board_events.text: Fast elimination: force (kg m s^{-2}) and energy (kg m^{2} s^{-2}) are VISIBLY built from others.
That leaves charge vs current. SI picked CURRENT as base.
Answer: (C) Electric current.

segments.text: <curious> Now a N E E T speed trap, and this one catches an enormous number of students every single year. Which one of the following is a base, or fundamental, quantity in the S I system? Option A, electric charge. Option B, force. Option C, electric current. Option D, energy.

Read those four again and feel the pull. Charge feels like it should be fundamental, doesn't it? It is such a basic, primitive idea — the thing electrons carry, the thing everything electrical is made of.

And that feeling is exactly the trap. Most students tick option A on pure reflex, in about two seconds, and get it wrong. In the S I, the chosen electrical base quantity is electric current, not charge.

Look at the board. On the green side, the fixed base list — and sitting there in the electrical slot is electric current, the ampere. On the red side, the derived ones, and charge is right at the top of them, written as coulomb equals ampere second.

Now let me show you how to kill this question in ten seconds without any agonising. Force is kilogram metre per second squared. Energy is kilogram metre squared per second squared. Both are visibly assembled out of other units — you can literally see the kilograms and metres in them. Both are derived. Options B and D are dead.

That leaves you with a straight fight: charge versus current. And here you do not reason, you recall. The S I picked current as the base quantity. Everything electrical — charge, voltage, resistance, everything — grows out of the ampere.

And here is the line that proves it. Current is charge per unit time, so charge is current times time. Which gives the coulomb as an ampere second. Charge is literally the product of a base unit and a base unit. It cannot itself be base.

So the answer is C, electric current. And the pitfall to carry away is this: fundamental in feeling is not the same as fundamental in the S I. The seven base quantities are a fixed, memorised list. Do not reason your way there from intuition — intuition is exactly what this question is weaponising against you.

<curious> अब एक N E E T speed trap, और यह हर साल बहुत भारी संख्या में students को पकड़ता है। इनमें से कौन सी S I system में base, यानी fundamental, quantity है? Option A, electric charge। Option B, force। Option C, electric current। Option D, energy।
इन चारों को दोबारा पढ़ो और खिंचाव महसूस करो। Charge को लगता है कि उसे fundamental होना ही चाहिए, है ना? इतनी basic, इतनी आदिम idea — जो electrons ढोते हैं, जिससे हर electrical चीज़ बनी है।
और वही feeling trap है। ज़्यादातर students दो सेकंड में reflex से option A पर tick लगाते हैं, और ग़लत हो जाते हैं। S I में चुनी गई electrical base quantity electric current है, charge नहीं।
Board देखो। हरी तरफ़ fixed base list — और electrical वाली जगह पर बैठी है electric current, ampere। लाल तरफ़ derived वाली, और charge उनमें सबसे ऊपर है, लिखा हुआ coulomb equals ampere second।

अब देखो इस सवाल को दस सेकंड में बिना तड़पे कैसे मारना है। Force है kilogram metre per second squared। Energy है kilogram metre squared per second squared। दोनों साफ़-साफ़ दूसरी units से जुड़कर बनी हैं — तुम्हें उनमें kilogram और metre दिख ही रहे हैं। दोनों derived। Options B और D ख़त्म।

अब बची सीधी लड़ाई: charge versus current। और यहाँ तुम reasoning नहीं करते, तुम याद करते हो। S I ने current को base quantity चुना। हर electrical चीज़ — charge, voltage, resistance, सब — ampere से निकलती है।

और यह रही वो line जो साबित करती है। Current है charge per unit time, तो charge है current into time। जिससे coulomb बनता है ampere second। Charge तो literally एक base unit और एक base unit का product है। वो ख़ुद base हो ही नहीं सकती।

तो answer है C, electric current। और साथ ले जाने वाली pitfall यह है: fundamental महसूस होना और S I में fundamental होना एक बात नहीं है। सात base quantities एक fixed, रटी हुई list हैं। Intuition से रास्ता मत निकालो — यह सवाल तो intuition को ही तुम्हारे ख़िलाफ़ हथियार बना रहा है।

sections.subtopic: Systems of Units and SI Units
sections.title: Example 3 [JEE Main]: surface tension from CGS to SI

board_events.text: [JEE Main] Convert 36 dyne cm^{-1} into SI units
Step 1 - dimensional formula. Surface tension = force per unit length.
Step 2 - CGS: M_1 = g, L_1 = cm, T_1 = s.   SI: M_2 = kg, L_2 = m, T_2 = s.
Surface tension = 0.036 N m^{-1}.
Sanity check: kg is a MUCH bigger mass unit than g, so the number must SHRINK. 36 becomes 0.036.

segments.text: J E E Main level now. A student measures the surface tension of a soap film as thirty six dyne per centimetre in the C G S system. Convert that value into S I units. This question is quietly testing two things at once: can you find a dimensional formula, and can you drive the conversion relation.
Step one, and this is the step everybody wants to skip. Find the dimensional formula of surface tension. Surface tension is defined as force per unit length.

So we take force, M L T to the minus two, and divide by a length, L. The L on top cancels against the L below, and we are left with M T to the minus two. Reading off the exponents against M to the a, L to the b, T to the c: a is one, b is zero, and c is minus two. Those three numbers are now our entire instruction set.

Step two, set up the two systems. In C G S, the mass unit is the gram, the length unit is the centimetre, the time unit is the second. In S I, mass is the kilogram, length is the metre, time is still the second.

Step three, plug into the master relation. The new number equals thirty six, times the mass ratio gram over kilogram raised to the power one, times the length ratio raised to the power zero, times the time ratio raised to the power minus two.

Now watch how much of that just evaporates. The length ratio is raised to the power zero, so it is one — length simply does not participate, because b came out zero. The time ratio is second over second, which is one, and one to any power is one. So the entire calculation collapses to thirty six times gram over kilogram. One gram is ten to the minus three kilograms, so we get thirty six times ten to the minus three, which is zero point zero three six.
So the surface tension is zero point zero three six newtons per metre.

And now do the check that costs you three seconds and saves you a mark. The kilogram is a far bigger mass unit than the gram. Bigger unit means the number should shrink. Thirty six went to zero point zero three six. It shrank. The answer survives the direction test, so we can sign off on it.

अब J E E Main level। एक student soap film का surface tension C G S system में छत्तीस dyne per centimetre नापता है। इस value को S I units में convert करो। यह सवाल चुपचाप दो चीज़ें एक साथ जाँच रहा है: dimensional formula निकाल सकते हो, और conversion relation चला सकते हो।
Step one, और यही वो step है जिसे हर कोई छोड़ना चाहता है। Surface tension का dimensional formula निकालो। Surface tension की definition है force per unit length।

तो force लो, M L T to the minus two, और एक length, L, से divide करो। ऊपर वाला L नीचे वाले L से cancel हो जाता है, और बचता है M T to the minus two। M to the a, L to the b, T to the c के सामने exponents पढ़ो: a है one, b है zero, और c है minus two। यही तीन numbers अब हमारा पूरा instruction set हैं।
Step two, दोनों systems set करो। C G S में mass unit है gram, length unit है centimetre, time unit है second। S I में mass है kilogram, length है metre, time अब भी second।

Step three, master relation में डालो। नया number बराबर छत्तीस, into mass ratio gram over kilogram raised to the power one, into length ratio raised to the power zero, into time ratio raised to the power minus two।

अब देखो इसमें से कितना ग़ायब हो जाता है। Length ratio पर power zero है, तो वो one है — length participate ही नहीं करती, क्योंकि b zero निकला। Time ratio है second over second, यानी one, और one की कोई भी power one होती है। तो पूरा calculation सिकुड़कर बचता है छत्तीस into gram over kilogram। एक gram है ten to the minus three kilogram, तो मिलता है छत्तीस into ten to the minus three, यानी zero point zero three six।
तो surface tension है zero point zero three six newton per metre।

और अब वो check करो जो तीन सेकंड लेता है और एक mark बचाता है। Kilogram, gram से कहीं बड़ी mass unit है। बड़ी unit मतलब number सिकुड़ना चाहिए। छत्तीस से zero point zero three six हो गया। सिकुड़ा। Answer direction test पास कर गया, तो इस पर दस्तख़त कर सकते हैं।

board_events.text: The Planck length - where gravity and quantum mechanics collide.

segments.text: J E E Advanced, and this is Procedure C made real. Suppose we build a natural system of units in which the speed of light c, the gravitational constant G, and Planck's constant h are each taken as fundamental and set numerically equal to one. Derive the expression for the unit of length in this system, and estimate its order of magnitude.

Step one. We declare that length must be some product of powers of our three fundamentals. So we write L equals c to the x, G to the y, h to the z, with three unknown exponents sitting there waiting to be pinned down.
There it is on the board: L equals c to the x, G to the y, h to the z. That is an assumption, and it is the only assumption we make. Everything from here is forced.

Look at the picture. Three constants go in at the top, each with its dimensional formula printed underneath it. The speed of light carries L T to the minus one. Big G carries M to the minus one, L cubed, T to the minus two. Planck's constant carries M, L squared, T to the minus one. Three recipes in, and one length has to come out.

Step two, insert the dimensional formulae and collect. On the left we want plain L, that is L to the power one. On the right, gather all the M's, all the L's, all the T's. The M exponent comes out as minus y plus z. The L exponent as x plus three y plus two z. The T exponent as minus x minus two y minus z.

Step three, and this is the rigorous core: match the exponents on both sides. The left side has no mass at all, so minus y plus z equals zero, which gives z equals y. The left side has no time at all, so minus x minus two y minus z equals zero, which gives x equals minus three y. And the left side has one power of length, so x plus three y plus two z equals one — substitute and it collapses to two y equals one. So y is one half, z is one half, and x is minus three halves.

Step four, assemble. L equals c to the minus three halves, G to the one half, h to the one half — which we tidy up into the square root of G h over c cubed. Put in the numbers, and it comes out around four times ten to the minus thirty five metres.

<excited> And look at what we just built out of nothing but bookkeeping. That is the Planck length — the scale at which gravity and quantum mechanics collide. We never did any physics. We just demanded that the dimensions balance. And notice this is exactly the logic the modern S I now uses: fix the constants, and every unit emerges automatically.

J E E Advanced, और यह Procedure C का असली रूप है। मान लो हम एक natural system of units बनाते हैं जिसमें speed of light c, gravitational constant G, और Planck's constant h — तीनों fundamental माने गए हैं और numerically one रख दिए गए हैं। इस system में unit of length का expression derive करो, और उसका order of magnitude estimate करो।

Step one। हम declare करते हैं कि length हमारे तीनों fundamentals की powers का कोई product होगी। तो लिखते हैं L equals c to the x, G to the y, h to the z, तीन unknown exponents ऊपर बैठे हुए, तय होने के इंतज़ार में।
Board पर वही है: L equals c to the x, G to the y, h to the z। यह एक assumption है, और यही इकलौता assumption है जो हम करते हैं। इसके आगे सब कुछ मजबूरी है।

Picture देखो। ऊपर से तीन constants अंदर जाते हैं, हर एक के नीचे उसका dimensional formula छपा है। Speed of light लाता है L T to the minus one। Big G लाता है M to the minus one, L cubed, T to the minus two। Planck's constant लाता है M, L squared, T to the minus one। तीन recipes अंदर, और एक length बाहर निकलनी ही है।

Step two, dimensional formulae डालो और इकट्ठा करो। बाईं तरफ़ हमें सीधा L चाहिए, यानी L to the power one। दाईं तरफ़ सारे M, सारे L, सारे T जमा करो। M का exponent निकलता है minus y plus z। L का exponent x plus three y plus two z। T का exponent minus x minus two y minus z।

Step three, और यही सख़्त core है: दोनों तरफ़ exponents match करो। बाईं तरफ़ mass है ही नहीं, तो minus y plus z equals zero, जिससे z equals y। बाईं तरफ़ time है ही नहीं, तो minus x minus two y minus z equals zero, जिससे x equals minus three y। और बाईं तरफ़ length की एक power है, तो x plus three y plus two z equals one — substitute करो और यह सिमटकर two y equals one बन जाता है। तो y है one half, z है one half, और x है minus three halves।

Step four, जोड़ो। L equals c to the minus three halves, G to the one half, h to the one half — जिसे साफ़ करके लिखते हैं square root of G h over c cubed। Numbers डालो, और लगभग चार into ten to the minus thirty five metre निकलता है।

<excited> और देखो हमने महज़ bookkeeping से क्या खड़ा कर दिया। यह Planck length है — वो scale जहाँ gravity और quantum mechanics टकराते हैं। हमने physics की ही नहीं। हमने बस ज़िद की कि dimensions बराबर हों। और ध्यान दो, आधुनिक S I ठीक यही logic इस्तेमाल करता है: constants fix कर दो, और हर unit अपने आप उभर आती है।

sections.subtopic: Systems of Units and SI Units
sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips: units and SI

board_events.text: Common student pitfalls
1. Calling charge, force or energy 'fundamental'. Only CURRENT is the electrical base quantity.
2. Sloppy symbols: 'kg' not 'Kg' or 'kgs'. 'K' = kelvin but 'k' = kilo. 'N' but 'newton'. 's' not 'sec'.
Unit symbols never take a plural 's' and never a full stop. Boards deduct marks for this.
3. Forgetting the dimensional POWER in conversions. Density [ML^{-3}] means the length ratio is CUBED.
4. Giving radian/steradian dimensions. They are dimensionless - treating them as length corrupts later work.
PRO-TIP: the two-step habit
Write the dimensional formula FIRST. Then plug mechanically. Then check: smaller unit means bigger number.

segments.text: Let me close this subtopic with the four ways students actually lose marks here, and then one habit that eliminates most of them.

Pitfall one, and we have already met it: calling charge, or force, or energy fundamental. Only electric current is the electrical base quantity. Memorise the seven base quantities as a fixed list and never, ever reason them out from intuition. Your intuition is the thing being tested against you.

Pitfall two is the silliest and the most expensive: sloppy unit symbols. It is k g in lowercase, not capital K g, and never k g s. Capital K is the kelvin, but lowercase k is the prefix kilo — completely different things. The symbol is capital N, but the name is newton with a small n. It is s, not s e c.

And two rules underneath those: unit symbols never take a plural s, and never take a full stop, except when the sentence itself ends. Boards genuinely deduct marks for this. It is free marks handed away for nothing.

Pitfall three is the number one conversion error in the whole chapter: forgetting the dimensional power. Converting a density means the length ratio must be cubed, because density carries M L to the minus three — length participates three times. Skip the cube and your answer is wrong by a factor of a million. This is not a small slip.

Pitfall four: giving radian and steradian dimensions. They are dimensionless. If you quietly treat them as carrying a length or an area, every dimensional analysis you attempt downstream is corrupted, and the corruption is invisible until your final answer is nonsense.
<whisper> Now the pro-tip, and this single habit is worth more than any formula on the board.

For any conversion whatsoever: write the dimensional formula first. Then plug mechanically into the master relation — mass ratio to the a, length ratio to the b, time ratio to the c. Then finish with the direction check: smaller unit implies bigger number. Write, plug, check. That one habit eliminates almost every conversion mistake in this chapter, in seconds, without any cleverness required.
इस subtopic को चार तरीक़ों से बंद करते हैं जिनसे students यहाँ सच में marks गँवाते हैं, और फिर एक आदत जो इनमें से ज़्यादातर को ख़त्म कर देती है।

पहली pitfall, और इससे हम मिल चुके हैं: charge, या force, या energy को fundamental कहना। सिर्फ़ electric current electrical base quantity है। सात base quantities को fixed list की तरह रटो और कभी, कभी भी intuition से मत निकालो। तुम्हारा intuition ही तो तुम्हारे ख़िलाफ़ जाँचा जा रहा है।

दूसरी pitfall सबसे बेवक़ूफ़ाना और सबसे महँगी है: लापरवाह unit symbols। यह छोटे अक्षरों में k g है, capital K g नहीं, और k g s तो कभी नहीं। Capital K है kelvin, पर छोटा k है prefix kilo — बिल्कुल अलग चीज़ें। Symbol है capital N, पर नाम है newton, छोटे n के साथ। यह s है, s e c नहीं।

और इनके नीचे दो नियम: unit symbols पर कभी plural s नहीं लगता, और कभी full stop नहीं, सिवाय तब जब sentence ख़ुद ख़त्म हो रहा हो। Boards इसके सच में marks काटते हैं। यह मुफ़्त के marks मुफ़्त में फेंकना है।

तीसरी pitfall पूरे chapter की नंबर एक conversion error है: dimensional power भूल जाना। Density convert करने का मतलब है length ratio cube होना ही चाहिए, क्योंकि density में M L to the minus three है — length तीन बार participate करती है। Cube छोड़ दिया तो answer दस लाख गुना ग़लत। यह कोई छोटी चूक नहीं है।

चौथी pitfall: radian और steradian को dimensions दे देना। वो dimensionless हैं। अगर तुमने चुपचाप मान लिया कि वो length या area लेकर चलती हैं, तो आगे की हर dimensional analysis ख़राब हो जाएगी, और यह ख़राबी तब तक दिखेगी नहीं जब तक final answer बकवास न निकल आए।
<whisper> अब pro-tip, और यह अकेली आदत board पर लिखे किसी भी formula से ज़्यादा क़ीमती है।

किसी भी conversion के लिए: पहले dimensional formula लिखो। फिर master relation में यंत्रवत plug करो — mass ratio to the a, length ratio to the b, time ratio to the c। फिर direction check से ख़त्म करो: छोटी unit मतलब बड़ा number। लिखो, plug करो, check करो। यही एक आदत इस chapter की लगभग हर conversion ग़लती को सेकंडों में ख़त्म कर देती है, बिना किसी चतुराई के।

board_events.caption: Quantities broken into their M, L, T ingredients

board_events.text: The list of 'how many parts of each base ingredient' = the DIMENSIONS of the quantity.
Written compactly with [M], [L], [T], [A], [K] - that is the DIMENSIONAL FORMULA.
m/s, km/h, furlongs per fortnight: the number changes. [LT^{-1}] does NOT.
Dimensions capture the NATURE of a quantity, stripped of which ruler you happened to use.

segments.text: Every physical quantity is, at heart, a blend of just a few ingredients: how much length is in it, how much mass, how much time.

Think of it like a recipe. A samosa is not a fundamental object. It is potato, plus flour, plus spices, in certain proportions. Nobody manufactures samosa from scratch as a primitive substance — you assemble it.

Physical quantities work exactly the same way. Speed is not fundamental. It is one part length, one part inverse-time — length divided by time. Force is one part mass, one part length, and two parts inverse-time.

Look at the board. Speed goes in, and what comes out the other side is one part L, one part one-over-T, which we write as L T to the minus one. Force gives M L T to the minus two. And look at strain, at the bottom — length divided by length, where every ingredient cancels and nothing survives at all.
That list — how many parts of each base ingredient a quantity contains — is what we call the dimensions of the quantity.

And writing it out compactly is its dimensional formula. We use square brackets, and the symbols M for mass, L for length, T for time, A for current, K for temperature. Speed has dimensional formula L T to the minus one. Force has M L T to the minus two.

Now here is the property that makes the whole thing powerful, and it is on the board in the yellow box. Whether you measure speed in metres per second, or kilometres per hour, or furlongs per fortnight, the number you write down changes completely. The dimensional formula does not. It is always L T to the minus one.

So dimensions capture the nature of a quantity, stripped of the accident of which ruler you happened to pick up that morning. Units are our changeable labels. Dimensions are something real and permanent underneath them.
हर physical quantity असल में बस कुछ ingredients का मिश्रण है: उसमें कितनी length है, कितना mass, कितना time।
इसे एक recipe की तरह सोचो। समोसा कोई fundamental चीज़ नहीं है। वो है आलू, plus मैदा, plus मसाले, तय अनुपात में। कोई समोसे को शुरू से एक आदिम पदार्थ की तरह नहीं बनाता — तुम उसे जोड़ते हो।

Physical quantities बिल्कुल ऐसे ही चलती हैं। Speed fundamental नहीं है। वो है एक हिस्सा length, एक हिस्सा inverse-time — length divided by time। Force है एक हिस्सा mass, एक हिस्सा length, और दो हिस्से inverse-time।

Board देखो। Speed अंदर जाती है, और दूसरी तरफ़ से निकलता है एक हिस्सा L, एक हिस्सा one-over-T, जिसे हम लिखते हैं L T to the minus one। Force देता है M L T to the minus two। और नीचे strain देखो — length divided by length, जहाँ हर ingredient cancel हो जाता है और कुछ भी नहीं बचता।
वही list — किसी quantity में हर base ingredient के कितने हिस्से हैं — उसी को हम उस quantity के dimensions कहते हैं।

और उसे संक्षेप में लिख देना ही उसका dimensional formula है। हम square brackets लगाते हैं, और symbols इस्तेमाल करते हैं — mass के लिए M, length के लिए L, time के लिए T, current के लिए A, temperature के लिए K। Speed का dimensional formula है L T to the minus one। Force का M L T to the minus two।

अब वो ख़ूबी सुनो जो इस पूरी चीज़ को ताक़तवर बनाती है, और वो board पर पीले box में लिखी है। तुम speed को metre per second में नापो, या kilometre per hour में, या furlongs per fortnight में — जो number तुम लिखोगे वो पूरी तरह बदल जाएगा। Dimensional formula नहीं बदलेगा। वो हमेशा L T to the minus one ही रहेगा।

तो dimensions किसी quantity की असली प्रकृति पकड़ते हैं, इस इत्तेफ़ाक़ से आज़ाद कि उस सुबह तुमने कौन सा ruler उठा लिया था। Units हमारे बदलते रहने वाले labels हैं। Dimensions उनके नीचे बैठी कोई असली और स्थायी चीज़ है।

sections.title: The principle of homogeneity: physics' spell-checker

board_events.text: You can only add or compare things of the SAME nature
You would never say '3 kilograms plus 5 seconds'. It is gibberish.
PRINCIPLE OF HOMOGENEITY: every term added, subtracted or equated must have IDENTICAL dimensions.

board_events.caption: One equation passes the check, one fails it instantly

board_events.text: This single rule lets you (1) check an equation, (2) derive a relation, (3) convert units.
Proofreading a friend's answer? Just check the recipe on the left matches the recipe on the right.
'Pressure = force x area'? [ML^{-1}T^{-2}] vs [ML^{3}T^{-2}]. Mismatch. Caught in five seconds.
Dimensional analysis is the physicist's spell-checker.

segments.text: Now here comes the single most powerful idea in this entire subtopic, and it rests on something you already know without being taught. You can only add or compare things of the same nature.
You would never say three kilograms plus five seconds. It is not wrong, exactly — it is gibberish. The sentence has no meaning at all. There is no answer, because the question is broken.

And that same rule governs every equation in physics. Every term that is added, subtracted, or equated must have identical dimensions. This is the principle of homogeneity of dimensions, and it is the engine behind everything we do in this subtopic.

Look at the board. On the green side: s equals u t plus half a t squared. The left side is a length. The first term on the right is a length. The second term on the right is a length. Every added term matches, so the equation is consistent, and it may be right. On the red side: pressure equals force times area. Left side is M L to the minus one T to the minus two. Right side is M L cubed T to the minus two. Mismatch. Dead on arrival.

That one rule buys you three separate powers. One, you can check whether an equation could possibly be right. Two, you can derive unknown relationships you were never taught. Three, you can convert a quantity between unit systems. All three, without doing the underlying physics in any detail at all.

<curious> Think about it this way. Imagine you are proofreading a friend's physics answer, and you do not have time to redo the whole problem. You can still catch a blunder instantly. Just check that the recipe on the left matches the recipe on the right.

Say your friend writes that pressure equals force times area. You check. Pressure is M L to the minus one T to the minus two. Force times area is M L T to the minus two, times L squared, which is M L cubed T to the minus two. Mismatch. You have caught the error in five seconds without knowing a single thing about the actual scenario.
That is what dimensional analysis is. The physicist's spell-checker. It does not tell you what the sentence should say. It just tells you, very fast, that this one cannot possibly be it.
अब आती है इस पूरे subtopic की सबसे ताक़तवर idea, और वो उस चीज़ पर टिकी है जो तुम्हें बिना सिखाए ही आती है। तुम सिर्फ़ एक ही तरह की चीज़ें जोड़ या compare कर सकते हो।
तुम कभी नहीं कहोगे तीन kilogram plus पाँच second। यह ग़लत नहीं है, ठीक-ठीक कहें तो — यह बकवास है। इस वाक्य का कोई मतलब ही नहीं। Answer इसलिए नहीं है क्योंकि सवाल ही टूटा हुआ है।

और यही नियम physics की हर equation पर राज करता है। जो भी term जोड़ा, घटाया या बराबर किया जा रहा है, उसके dimensions एक जैसे होने ही चाहिए। यही principle of homogeneity of dimensions है, और इस subtopic में हम जो कुछ भी करते हैं उसका engine यही है।

Board देखो। हरी तरफ़: s equals u t plus half a t squared। बाईं तरफ़ length। दाईं तरफ़ पहला term length। दूसरा term भी length। हर जुड़ने वाला term match करता है, तो equation consistent है, और शायद सही हो। लाल तरफ़: pressure equals force into area। बाईं तरफ़ M L to the minus one T to the minus two। दाईं तरफ़ M L cubed T to the minus two। Mismatch। पहुँचते ही ख़त्म।

यह एक नियम तुम्हें तीन अलग ताक़तें देता है। एक, तुम जाँच सकते हो कि कोई equation सही हो भी सकती है या नहीं। दो, तुम ऐसे relationships derive कर सकते हो जो तुम्हें कभी पढ़ाए ही नहीं गए। तीन, तुम quantity को एक unit system से दूसरे में convert कर सकते हो। तीनों, बिना नीचे की physics में गहराई से घुसे।

<curious> इसे ऐसे सोचो। मान लो तुम दोस्त का physics answer proofread कर रहे हो, और पूरा problem दोबारा करने का time नहीं है। फिर भी तुम गड़बड़ तुरंत पकड़ सकते हो। बस check करो कि बाईं तरफ़ की recipe दाईं तरफ़ की recipe से match करती है या नहीं।

मान लो दोस्त ने लिखा pressure equals force into area। तुम check करते हो। Pressure है M L to the minus one T to the minus two। Force into area है M L T to the minus two, into L squared, यानी M L cubed T to the minus two। Mismatch। तुमने पाँच सेकंड में error पकड़ ली, और असली scenario के बारे में तुम्हें एक शब्द भी नहीं पता।
यही dimensional analysis है। Physicist का spell-checker। वो नहीं बताता कि वाक्य क्या होना चाहिए। वो बस बहुत तेज़ी से बता देता है कि यह वाला तो हो ही नहीं सकता।

sections.title: Not a classroom trick: predicting physics you were never taught

board_events.text: The same check, run in reverse, PREDICTS physics
Know that a quantity depends on a few others? Demand that the recipes balance.
That demand often forces the relationship almost entirely into shape...
...leaving only an unknown pure number out front.
Physicists estimated the energy of an atomic explosion this way - before doing the full theory.
Also: the speed of ripples on water. The pulsation rate of a star. All from balancing recipes.
Any ratio of two similar things is DIMENSIONLESS: strain, refractive index, relative density.

segments.text: So far dimensional analysis sounds like a defensive tool — a way of catching other people's mistakes. But what makes it genuinely powerful, rather than just a classroom trick, is that the same check runs in reverse.

Suppose you know that some quantity depends on a few others, but you have no idea how. You do not know the physics. You have not been taught the derivation. All you do is demand that the recipes balance on both sides.

And here is the astonishing part: that single demand often forces the relationship almost entirely into shape. Not partly. Almost completely. The exponents get pinned down, one by one, with no choice left in the matter.
What it leaves behind is one unknown pure number sitting out front — a two, or a pi, or a two pi. That is the only thing the method cannot see. The structure, it hands you for free.

Physicists have used exactly this reasoning to estimate the energy released by an atomic explosion, long before anyone did the full hydrodynamic theory. Just from the radius of the blast, the time, and the density of the air.

The same trick gives the speed of ripples on water, and the pulsation rate of a star — which we will actually derive ourselves, later in this very subtopic. So do not treat dimensions as a chore. Treat them as a fast, surprisingly deep first weapon you reach for whenever a relation is unknown or a formula looks suspicious.

One more consequence worth pocketing now. Any quantity that is a ratio of two similar things comes out dimensionless. Strain is length over length. Refractive index is speed over speed. Relative density is density over density. In every case the ingredients cancel perfectly.

So on the board: strain equals L over L, which is M to the zero, L to the zero, T to the zero. Pure number. Remember this family — dimensionless quantities show up constantly, and recognising one instantly is often the whole of a question.

अब तक dimensional analysis एक defensive tool जैसा लग रहा है — दूसरों की ग़लतियाँ पकड़ने का तरीक़ा। लेकिन जो चीज़ इसे सच में ताक़तवर बनाती है, महज़ classroom trick नहीं, वो यह है कि यही check उल्टी दिशा में भी चलता है।

मान लो तुम्हें पता है कि कोई quantity कुछ दूसरी quantities पर depend करती है, पर कैसे — इसका कोई अंदाज़ा नहीं। Physics नहीं आती। Derivation पढ़ाई नहीं गई। तुम बस इतना करते हो कि ज़िद करते हो कि दोनों तरफ़ की recipes बराबर हों।
और यह रहा चौंकाने वाला हिस्सा: वही अकेली ज़िद अक्सर relationship को लगभग पूरी तरह shape में ढाल देती है। थोड़ा नहीं। लगभग पूरा। Exponents एक-एक करके तय हो जाते हैं, कोई विकल्प बचता ही नहीं।
पीछे बचता है सिर्फ़ एक unknown शुद्ध number, सामने बैठा हुआ — कोई two, या pi, या two pi। बस यही एक चीज़ है जो यह method नहीं देख पाता। Structure तो वो मुफ़्त में दे देता है।
Physicists ने ठीक इसी reasoning से atomic explosion से निकली energy का estimate लगाया था, उससे बहुत पहले कि किसी ने पूरी hydrodynamic theory की हो। बस blast की radius, time, और हवा की density से।

यही trick पानी की लहरों की speed देती है, और किसी तारे की pulsation rate भी — जिसे हम इसी subtopic में आगे ख़ुद derive करेंगे। तो dimensions को बोझ मत समझो। इन्हें वो तेज़, हैरान कर देने वाला गहरा पहला हथियार समझो जो तुम तब उठाते हो जब relation अनजान हो या कोई formula संदिग्ध लगे।

एक और नतीजा जेब में रख लो। जो भी quantity दो एक जैसी चीज़ों का ratio है, वो dimensionless निकलती है। Strain है length over length। Refractive index है speed over speed। Relative density है density over density। हर मामले में ingredients पूरी तरह cancel हो जाते हैं।

तो board पर: strain equals L over L, यानी M to the zero, L to the zero, T to the zero। शुद्ध number। इस परिवार को याद रखो — dimensionless quantities लगातार आती रहती हैं, और किसी एक को तुरंत पहचान लेना अक्सर पूरा सवाल ही होता है।

sections.title: Where the method goes blind - the five sharp boundaries

board_events.text: This power comes with sharp boundaries. Examiners test them relentlessly.
